test_title: PYST 13: SSC CGL 2025 Tier-I Similar Paper - Quantitative Aptitude (Held On: 16th Sep 2025 Shift 1)
subject: maths
question: A right-angled triangle is inscribed in a circle with a diameter of 26 cm. If one of the legs of the triangle measures 10 cm, what is the length of the altitude drawn to the hypotenuse?
solution:
**Given:**

Diameter of the circle = 26 cm

One leg of the triangle = 10 cm

**Formula Used:**

Hypotenuse = Diameter of the circle

Pythagoras theorem: Hypotenuse² = Leg 1² + Leg 2²

Area of triangle = (1/2) × Base × Height

Area of triangle = (1/2) × Hypotenuse × Altitude

**Calculation:**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/5d346824f9e992b79e6857d3e7c04e6ea8d4193a0d97892bff8ae75236479576.png] 

⇒ Hypotenuse = Diameter = 26 cm

⇒ Hypotenuse² = 26²

⇒ 26² = 10² + Leg 2²

⇒ 676 = 100 + Leg 2²

⇒ Leg 2² = 676 − 100

⇒ Leg 2² = 576

⇒ Leg 2 = √576

⇒ Leg 2 = 24 cm

Area of triangle:

⇒ (1/2) × Base × Height = (1/2) × Hypotenuse × Altitude

⇒ (1/2) × 10 × 24 = (1/2) × 26 × Altitude

⇒ 120 = 13 × Altitude

⇒ Altitude = 120 / 13

⇒ Altitude ≈ 9.23 cm

**∴ The correct answer is 9.23 cm.**
